newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. Fed's Greenspan arrives in China for talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed's Greenspan arrives in China for talks.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan arrived in Beijing on Wednesday for two days of meetings with China's most senior finance and banking officials.

Greenspan is making his second visit to China at the invitation of the central bank, the People's Bank of China, and is due to hold talks on Wednesday with China's economic tsar, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji.
He will then hold talks with Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China.

On Thursday, Greenspan is due to meet Chen Jinhua, chairman of the State Planning Commission, as well as Finance Minister Liu Zhongli and President and Communist Party leader Jiang Zemin before leaving early on Friday for Tokyo.
Greenspan declined to speak to reporters on arrival at Beijing's Capital Airport.

Chinese central bank officials said the trip was part of normal exchanges with the Federal Reserve, which has had a cooperative relationship with China's central bank for more than a decade, offering technical exchanges and training.
